Then all those dragon kings rose from their seats;
each adjusted his robes, bared his right shoulder,
and with palms joined toward the Buddha, [offered] various kinds of immeasurable, boundless, and incalculable numbers [of offerings].
Subtle and exquisite fragrant flowers, unguents, and powdered incense;
flower garlands, garments, precious banners, flags, and canopies;
dragon-flowers, jeweled crowns, and pearl necklaces.
With nets of precious flowers, silken fabrics, and pearls,
they covered the Tathāgata and performed various musical performances,
giving rise to a heart of profound reverence and extraordinary wonder.
Having circumambulated the Buddha to the right, they withdrew and stood to one side.
At that time, the nāgas conceived this aspiration:
"May all the oceans of worlds throughout the entire universe..."
The ocean of bodies of subtle atoms;
the ocean of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas;
pervading all oceans of worlds.
They have already passed beyond all oceans of atoms of the four great elements— earth, water, fire,
and wind— as well as all oceans of atoms of the images of all forms.
Having already passed through immeasurable, inconceivable, and ineffable numbers of *asaṃkhyeya* oceans of various bodies,
they manifest within a single body an ocean-like cloud of immeasurable *asaṃkhyeya* hands.
Pervading the ten directions, and furthermore, from within each and every particle of dust, we manifest immeasurable clouds and oceans of offerings that fill the ten directions.
We all hold these forth as offerings to the ocean-like assemblies of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.
Immeasurable, innumerable, inconceivable, and ineffable asaṃkhyeya clouds of the physical bodies of Samantabhadra’s practices and vows, uninterrupted and pervasive,
abide filling the limits of space.
In this way, there are oceans of clouds of the Bodhisattvas’ form-bodies;
oceans of clouds of the palaces and sites of enlightenment of all suns, moons, and bodies, radiant with the colors of all varieties of jewels;
and oceans of clouds of all jewel garlands.
With ocean-clouds of pavilions that are treasuries of the radiance of all jewels;
with ocean-clouds of trees that are treasuries of all powdered incense;
and with ocean-clouds manifesting all colors through all kinds of unguents and burning incense.
With oceans of clouds of all kinds of musical sounds produced by striking instruments;
with oceans of clouds of all kinds of fragrant trees;
and with such other things as these—immeasurable, boundless, inconceivable, and unspeakable in number, reaching into the incalculable (*asaṃkhyeya*).
Such oceans of clouds of offerings as these fill the reaches of space. We all together offer worship,
pay homage, show respect, and revere this ocean-like assembly of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.

filling the reaches of space,

At that time, the dragon kings and others, having made this vow, [proceeded].
They circumambulated the Buddha three times and prostrated themselves with their heads at his feet.
Having received the Buddha’s holy command, they each returned to their respective places and sat down in order.
At that time, there was a dragon king named Anantavyūha-sāgaramegha-tejorājacakravarti.
As the lord of a trichiliocosm,
because he dwells in the power of non-retrogression through his vows,
he desires to make offerings, pay homage, and prostrate to the Tathāgata, and to listen to and receive the true Dharma.
Having come to this Jambudvīpa,
that nāga king rose from his seat,
adjusted his robes, and bared his right shoulder.
Placing his right knee on the ground and joining his palms toward the Buddha,
he addressed the Buddha, saying: "World-Honored One, I now wish to ask a few questions."
"Tathāgata, the Perfectly All-Knowing One, I only pray that you will grant me your permission.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the Dragon King Vīryatejaś-cakravarti-maṇḍala-ghana-megha, saying:
“Great Dragon King, if you have any doubts, feel free to ask whatever you wish.
I shall analyze and explain them for you so that your mind may rejoice.
When he had spoken these words, the Dragon King Boundless Adornment Ocean-Cloud Majestic Virtue Wheel Canopy addressed the Buddha, saying:
"Indeed, World-Honored One, how can you cause all the dragon kings to extinguish all suffering and obtain peace and happiness?
Having obtained peace and happiness, you may further cause sweet rain to fall upon this Jambudvīpa at the proper time."
All trees, forests, medicinal herbs, and crops shall grow with abundant flavor,
causing all the people of Jambudvīpa to experience complete happiness.
At that time, having heard these words, the World-Honored One addressed the Great Dragon King Anantavyūha-sāgara-megha-tejo-rāja-cakravarti-pariśuddhacchattra, saying:
"Excellent, excellent! You now act for the benefit of those sentient beings."
That you are able to ask the Tathāgata such matters as these—
Great Dragon King, listen well, listen thoroughly, and listen most attentively.
You should apply your mind, and I shall speak for you.
Nāga King, you have accomplished one dharma by which all nāgas eliminate every suffering and become fully endowed with peace and happiness.
What is this one dharma? It is the practice of loving-kindness (maitrī).
Great Dragon King, if there are gods or humans who practice great loving-kindness,
fire cannot burn them, weapons cannot harm them,
water cannot sweep them away, and poisons cannot affect them.
Neither internal nor external enemies will be able to invade or disturb them;
they shall sleep in peace and awaken in peace,
their bodies sustained by the protection of their own merit.
By virtue of great merit, one attains majestic power and is not oppressed by others;
among humans and devas, one’s physical form is upright and dignified, and one is loved and respected by all;
wherever one goes, there is no obstruction whatsoever.
All sufferings are extinguished and removed, the mind attains joy, and all forms of happiness are fully possessed.
By the power of great compassion, after the end of life, one will be reborn in the Brahma world.
O Great Dragon King, if there are devas or humans...
By practicing the conduct of great loving-kindness, one obtains such benefits and merit;
therefore, O Dragon King, you should practice with a body of loving-kindness, speech of loving-kindness, and mind of loving-kindness.
Furthermore, O Dragon Kings,
there is a dhāraṇī named "Bestowing Peace and Happiness upon All Sentient Beings.
You dragons must constantly recite it, maintain mindfulness of it, and uphold it.
It is able to extinguish all the suffering and afflictions of the nāgas and bestow peace and happiness upon them.
Once those nāgas have obtained such happiness,
they are then able to send down sweet rain upon Jambudvīpa in accordance with the proper seasons.
It causes all trees, forests, medicinal herbs, and crops to grow and flourish.
At that time, the Dragon King again addressed the Buddha, saying:
"What is called the dhāraṇī phrase for bestowing all happiness?"
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke this dhāraṇī, saying: *tadyathā | dhāraṇi dhāraṇi | uddhāraṇi | sampratiṣṭhite*.
